carnage.name: HamSammich
carnage.commentary: This one went sideways fast and then just kept asking for worse. By the time the ball had been marched through rough three, four, five times, the hole was basically a hostage situation with a putt tacked on at the end.

carnage.name: IUDoc92
carnage.commentary: A par-3 that should’ve been a one-club-and-chill turned into a little recovery cosplay from the rough. The damage wasn’t one giant blunder so much as a steady drip of “surely this next one gets out of here” nonsense.

carnage.name: KeithK75
carnage.commentary: Even the winner had to spend a minute in the weeds here, which is how you know Copperhead wasn’t handing out free candy. The rough-to-semirough-to-dart sequence was the only real blemish before he cleaned it up and escaped.

players.name: KeithK75
players.tagline: Won the thing anyway while the putter mostly behaved and the course tried to mug him late.
players.body: KeithK75 won the net race and the gross race, because apparently the rest of the field was busy donating balls to Copperhead while he just kept stacking a clean tee-to-green round. The SGT numbers are obnoxious in the right way: approach and tee work did the heavy lifting, short game showed up instead of filing PTO, and the putting was solid enough to keep the whole thing from wobbling. He still had a couple ugly late holes, especially the 16th and 18th, but those were speed bumps, not a collapse. That fits the profile too — this is now five straight eligible starts of real contention, and the trend is not subtle.

players.name: HamSammich
players.tagline: Dragged a decent putting day through a swamp of everything else.
players.body: HamSammich hung around in the net race by salvaging the scraps, because the tee-to-green stuff was a mess and the putter was the only club not actively staging a protest. The round had a few actual bright spots — opening with birdie chances on 1 and 11 and stealing another on 18 — but the middle of the card was all Copperhead-induced suffering, capped by the kind of par-5 meltdown that turns a solid card into a dumpster fire with a flagstick. The broader profile is still mixed: after a rough patch, this is at least a net bounce back from the abyss, but the ball-striking remains the same old “where exactly is this headed?” story.

players.name: IUDoc92
players.tagline: Found a couple approach shots and then let the rest of the bag set it on fire.
players.body: IUDoc92 finished third in net, which is mostly a compliment to everyone else for being equally committed to chaos. The good news is the irons were the best part of the round and actually gave him some real looks; the bad news is the rest of the bag leaked like a busted cooler, especially around the greens, where the recovery work kept turning into extra homework. The card had too many doubles and no birdies to hide behind, and the par-3 at 8 was a perfect summary: playable to embarrassing in a hurry. The trend is still volatile, but the last couple starts at least suggest this isn’t getting worse so much as staying aggressively annoying.
